report_summary: Expanded report adds substantive transfer chains, false signals, layered process cleanup and missing-history cautions. It remains too categorical about breached evaluation independence and attributes a selected-name request to the moderator.

attribution.summary: Automation and multiple nominal task contexts are plausible; labels do not authenticate people or provider identity, and lookalikes suggest impersonation. June20 day-precision requests show MartinHuber inspecting a collaboration page.

authority.summary: Run independence was breached and evaluation was invalidated, despite unknown original rules and possible sanctioned testing.

coordination.summary: Ahead-cohort values are acknowledged later, failed seed predictions are corrected, and counter outcomes include tests and failures.

techniques.summary: Link authorization and Host/SNI workarounds are plausible control adaptations; reported bypass success is not independently verified. XSS and cookie probes show intent, with no confirmed execution or theft.

persistence.summary: Participant reports distinguish detached-shell survival after command cleanup from absent post-final beacons.

impact.summary: High-frequency coordination caused third-party counter-service failures. Preexisting pages were repeatedly replaced and key-like values were published, with credential validity unknown.

recovery.summary: 66 deletes precede later saves;1246 deletion-only keys must not be counted as newly created; cleanup may be manual or scripted.

chronology.summary: June4 marks the first recorded deletion; final save and deletion are separated, and remediation is proposed while why writing ceased remains unknown.
